newsitem.title: ROMANIA: BUCHAREST BOURSE TRADING THIN, RECOVERY SEEN AHEAD.
newsitem.headline: BUCHAREST BOURSE TRADING THIN, RECOVERY SEEN AHEAD.

text.p: Bucharest stocks traded mixed on Wednesday, with buying interest remaining light and the market drifting slightly up mostly on marginal rises in blue chips.
Three independent indices, the VAB, the BIG and the CAS-SE, based on average prices and market capitalisation, edged up by 0.5, 0.38 and 0.48 percent respectively from Tuesday.

"Trading was thin, with volumes and turnover on the slide. Signs of a slight reinvigoration are in the air and we might see volumes rise after new foreign investment procedures become effective," a broker said.
Romania's central bank on Wednesday approved long-awaited norms regulating repatriation in foreign investment.

Non-residents acting as foreign investors are given access to the local foreign exchange market where they can submit spot or forward hard currency buying and selling orders related to their investments in Romania.
The norms, which follow a June government decree on free repatriation of profits, initial investment and capital gains, have to be published in the Official Gazette to be effective.
Stock exchange volume on Wednesday fell to 1.9 million shares from 2.1 million the previous day. Turnover was some 1.5 billion lei, down from 8.8 billion.

The first tier dominated trading, with 1.2 million shares in volume and around six billion lei in turnover. Most of the nine high-caps gained on their average prices but only three managed to close higher in stronger late-trading pressure.
Antibiotice ATBE.BX pharmaceutical closed at 7,400 lei, 150 stronger on the previous session. Traders said most of the 309 deals in Antibiotice were struck by foreign investors.
Azomures fertiliser maker firmed 100 lei to 3,550, after spending most of the day at a lower quote. Oltchim rose 50 lei to 3,900 and Compa COPA.BX spare parts maker ended 50 lei higher at 2,400.
